text:
lina: Heads up — hit a problem during a config rollback test. We have a nested flag dependency where parent flag rollback succeeds but child flag stays stuck at new value. Not sure if it's a race in the apply path or in the operator reconciliation.
ashwin: ugh. repro steps? quick diff or snippet?
lina: repro = create parent P (enabled->false) with child C scoped to P. Flip parent back to true, then rollback parent to previous false. Parent shows false in console, child shows true in backend. Happens intermittently (~1/20).
ashwin: can you paste the api call payload you used? think about ETag/compare-and-set.
lina: payloads are like: ```json
{
  "id": "P",
  "enabled": false,
  "children": ["C"],
  "_etag": "abc123"
}
``` then child updated separately. We used two sequential PUTs (parent then child).
tegris-bot: deploy-check: rollout-safety-policy v2 active — dry-run flag apply allowed + audit logs enabled.
samir: two quick theories: 1) apply is async and parent rollback triggers a cascade reconcile that uses cached view of child and doesn't requeue child update, 2) we have an ordering bug in the console bulk-edit where parent change marked completed before children finish.
olivia: agree with samir. For (1) maybe we need stronger transactional semantics for dependent ops: server should track dependency graph and ensure child nodes are reconciled before marking parent applied. Could add an orchestration phase 'await-children' with a bounded timeout and automatic queueing.
ashwin: on API side we could support a param `cascade_sync=true` that the console sets for rollback flows. That would convert two PUTs into a single server-side operation: ```http
POST /api/configs/rollback?cascade_sync=true
{ "target": "P", "to": "v123" }
``` server would then run dependency resolution and apply children in the same transaction-like operation (best-effort).
lina: that would help. Concern: we need telemetry to show when cascade_sync falls back to async because of timeout. Otherwise ops won't know rollbacks partially completed.
samir: telemetry plan: emit an event `config.rollback.cascade` with fields: success|partial|timeout, affected_count, duration_ms. Console should surface partial/timeout as toast + link to audit timeline.
olivia: UX ask: default cascade_sync=false for API users, but Console rollback flow should set it true and show a progress modal that polls `GET /api/configs/ops/{op_id}`. If op_id ends in partial, show a one-click rollback-forward to previous stable and open a ticket template.
nashwin: implementation note — be careful of cycles in dependency graph. We'll need cycle-detection and a safe-escape: if cycle detected, return 409 with a human-friendly message and list of nodes.
lina: I can prototype console modal and a short backend PoC that performs dependency ordering + limited waiting.
tegris-bot: reminder: please add tests for idempotency and flaky requeues (team: @eng-platform).
nashwin: ok i'll add api schema for cascade_sync and the op status contract. Can we aim for a small RFC by EOD tomorrow?
olivia: yes. I'll draft UX copy for partial state and the ticket template.
samir: I'll own telemetry + alert rule (SLO breach if >1% rollbacks partial over 1h).
lina: thanks — will drop a short thread in #release-war-room when prototype ready. :thumbsup:
